reader.requirement: At 85 the compiler must accept, and run as one separate OPEN per file-name, an OPEN statement whose file-names (in any of the INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND phrases) have different organizations (sequential, relative, indexed) and different access modes (sequential, random, dynamic), each file getting its own open mode and I-O status.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the 2002 OPEN SHARING phrase (COBOL0900) below 2002; the mixed-organization list itself is not gated
only the citation text of the FORMAT-clause diagnostic (DialectLevel); the per-file SR1 EXTEND/access check is edition-agnostic
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility: at 85 every connector opens as ALL OTHER and Table 19 is not asked, so sibling connectors opened by one OPEN never arbitrate against one another

reader.edition-search: grep of OpenStatement/openClause in the compiler (VersionConformancePass, StatementBinder, SequentialIoBinder, EcBinder.ExceptionPerform), DialectLevel/Edition in SequentialIoEmitter and the runtime IO folder
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the admission of mixed organizations and access modes is the same code at 85 and 2023; only the SHARING phrase (refused at 85) and the default sharing mode differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf23_03 mixes three organizations under OUTPUT and INPUT only; the I-O and EXTEND phrases mixed in one statement, and one file's failed open beside successful ones, are not exercised

reader.notes: The binder loops each open group and file-name, resolving and screening each file on its own (CheckOpenModeForFile) with no cross-file organization or access comparison, and BindOpen returns one BoundOpen per file (an implicit series), so a mixed list compiles and runs file by file. Probes cover I-O and EXTEND groups mixed with relative, indexed and sequential files in one statement and a failed open beside successful ones.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR1/SR2, GR1 Table 1, GR17 (separate OPEN per file in order) and the Sequential I-O OPEN format §1985:VII.4.3.2 (REVERSED, WITH NO REWIND beside other files). Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-163/runs: r1ext-002 (OPEN OUTPUT FQ WITH NO REWIND FR FX; one EXTEND phrase over sequential, relative-sequential and indexed-sequential files; OPEN INPUT FQ WITH NO REWIND FR FX) printed OUT 07 00 00 / EXT 00 00 00 / RK=0002 / WR 00 00 00 / INP 07 00 00 / Q=BBBBBB / R=R2R2R2 RK=0002 / X=X02YYY, each file run on its own; r1order-001 (USE ERROR ON INPUT, OPEN INPUT FQ FM(missing relative random) FX(indexed dynamic)) printed DA Q=00 M=35 X=ZZ / AFTER Q=00 M=35 X=00, so the files open one by one in the written order with the declarative between them (GR17); r1rev-001 (OPEN INPUT FQ REVERSED FM FX) gives the same output, the 1985 sequential-only REVERSED phrase admitted beside relative and indexed files. Without INVALID KEY/AT END the first r1ext run was refused per file by COBOL6826 (VIII.4.9.3 SR3, IX.4.9.3 SR3, VII.4.4.3 SR2), unrelated to mixing. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR2 the text is in SR2; OK §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR17 the text is in GR17; OK §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR4 the text is in SR4.
